assertions: Forced base64 polling returns bytes 0...4; observer sees bAAECAwQ= in the actual POST body.

Direct WebSocket and completed polling-to-WebSocket upgrade return bytes 0...4 and empty Data. Actual client frames are base64 text, not binary frames; handshake requests b64=1. Native Data replaces ArrayBuffer/Blob.
Native Data replaces Blob input/output. Bytes 0...4 and zero-length bytes survive the raw polling round trip in order; the engine API uses a separate text header.

Five payloads at the original 72/20/20/20/72-byte boundaries are echoed in order. Every actual polling POST is at most the 100-byte advertised maxPayload. Includes base64 expansion and record separators.
Native Data replaces Blob input/output. WebSocket echoes bytes 0...4 and empty bytes; observer confirms binary frames, independently of the Socket.IO parser.
Raw localhost polling opens, then receives the unsolicited server greeting hi. Open precedes message delivery and the engine has a nonempty SID.
Raw localhost WebSocket opens, then receives the unsolicited server greeting hi. Open precedes message delivery and the engine has a nonempty SID.
The exact upstream string cash money followed by three euro symbols is echoed unchanged through raw polling.
The exact upstream Unicode scalar sequence U+10000 through U+10FFFF and private-use endpoints U+E000/U+F8FF is echoed unchanged, not merely a common emoji.
addTrailingSlash(false) emits /engine.io? on the wire, with no slash before the query. Custom paths are normalized independently of option order; the default retains the slash.

Server-set cookies are sent on subsequent polling POSTs and on the WebSocket upgrade only when enabled. The isolated jar survives reconnect and is not shared with another engine or the application jar.
Disabled credentials do not resend server cookies in polling or the WebSocket upgrade, and do not read a pre-populated engine jar. Explicit application Cookie headers remain explicit.
Foundation parses the upstream simple foo=bar cookie into the same name and value. The native cookie object and browser CORS semantics are not claimed to be identical to the Node CookieJar.
Foundation preserves the entire upstream cookie value bar=bar&foo=foo&John=Doe&Doe=John, including equals signs and ampersands.
A 101-byte payload against maxHttpBufferSize=100 produces polling write error HTTP 413 and a transport error close carrying structured detail.
A 101-byte WebSocket payload against maxHttpBufferSize=100 closes with peer code 1009. A simultaneous receive error must not erase the peer close code or turn it into a generic error close.
An actual stale-SID polling GET reports HTTP 400 and the exact Session ID unknown JSON body, followed by one detailed transport error close.
An actual stale-SID WebSocket handshake fails and closes with native transport detail. URLSession need not expose the HTTP rejection status; no fabricated XHR or CloseEvent object is claimed.
A custom extraHeaders value reaches both actual polling GET and POST requests. URLSession replaces browser/Node XMLHttpRequest; browser CORS/preflight is not implemented by this native test.

Original two-zero-byte ArrayBuffer payload is represented by Data at namespace /, id 0. Exact header and attachment bytes also have an independent assertion; native encode/decode preserves the payload.
Original typed-array bytes 0...4 survive Data encoding at namespace / and id 0. A sliced buffer excludes sentinel prefix/suffix bytes without modifying its source.
Original two-zero-byte Blob payload is adapted to native Data at namespace / and id 0; empty and high-bit byte payloads also round-trip.
The original nested hi/why/binary/bye event at /deep with id 999 encodes and reconstructs unchanged using Data instead of Blob. Additional null/nested inputs remain intact.
The original hi ack/why/binary/bye ack payload at /deep with id 999 encodes as a binary ACK and reconstructs unchanged using Data instead of Blob.
All seven public native SocketPacket.PacketType values correspond to protocol type numbers 0 through 6.

The standalone JS parseuri helper exposes a parsed-component object and handles a corpus of shorthand inputs. Swift uses Foundation URL/URLComponents instead; no identical public parseuri result or input grammar is promised. Absolute transport URL validation remains separately tested.
